description: I am a Software Engineering with Artificial Intelligence student, passionate about building innovative technology and experienced in creating solutions that combine traditional software development with machine learning models, computer vision, and multi-agent systems. Throughout my academic journey, I have led and collaborated on diverse tech projects, ranging from desktop applications and backend architectures to intelligent systems applied to simulation and visual recognition.
summary: AstraSync is a web-based health self-assessment tool for astronauts on long-duration missions. Astronauts enter heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, body temperature, sleep and mood. Each indicator gets a color-coded status (normal / attention / contact flight surgeons) with plain-language instructions on how to measure it and what to do next. A clickable human figure shows how spaceflight affects each body system (brain, heart, metabolism, immune system, bones and muscles), and a hazard map links the indicators to NASA HRP's five hazards: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields and hostile closed environments. The app also includes micro-interventions (guided breathing, sleep clock, reflex test), a 3D orbital viewer, and PDF/JSON/CSV report export, in English and Spanish. It matters because on missions far from Earth, crews must detect health changes themselves and know when to ask for ground support. Reference ranges are orientative, not clinical, and telemetry is simulated.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Astronauts log six health indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood). Each one is evaluated against reference ranges and shown as green / yellow / red. Yellow gives a concrete action to take on board; red adds a recommendation to inform ground flight surgeons. Every indicator explains how to measure it and why it matters in space.

HOW IT USES NASA RESEARCH: We mapped the indicators to the five hazards of human spaceflight from NASA's Human Research Program. Each hazard card shows the status of the indicators it affects. A clickable body figure explains what each system does, how spaceflight affects it (fluid shifts, bone loss, immune changes, behavioral health) and what the astronaut can do.

EXTRA FEATURES: guided breathing and audio (Neuro-Reset), sleep clock, reflex test, mission tasks, a 3D orbital viewer, configurable heart-rate alerts, and report export (PDF, JSON, CSV). Bilingual (EN/ES).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT: Helps crews notice health changes early, understand them without medical training, and decide when to escalate, which matters most when communication with Earth is delayed.

TOOLS: JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Vite [add the 3D library from package.json]. Data entered is stored only in the browser.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED: Reference ranges are general guidance, not clinical diagnosis. Telemetry in the dashboard is simulated; the health assessment module uses user-entered measurements. The tool is not a medical device. Radiation dose cannot be self-measured, so radiation is tracked indirectly through immune-related signs.

SI USE: Code and text were developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).
